subject: Proposed MAP retarget & final acceptance window — Helios Health
messages:
From: jasmine_liu@redwood.com
To: Sam Carter <scarter@helioshealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 08 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed MAP & acceptance window for Q2 evaluation

Sam —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Attached is a draft Mutual Action Plan (MAP) that aligns Redwood's evaluation milestones with Helios's test windows. High level proposes:

- Week 1: Contract redlines complete (legal + procurement)
- Week 2–3: Integration + smoke tests (staged dataset)
- Week 4: Performance eval & quality sign-off
- Week 5: Final acceptance window and go/no-go decision

Two small asks before I lock dates: confirm the procurement approval cycle (how many approvers) and whether you need a dedicated SOC2 evidence drop for your security review.

I've attached the MAP and a condensed evaluation checklist for your engineering team to share with Alex. If we can agree to the schedule this week, we can reserve dedicated Dedicated capacity for your eval in mid-April, which helps keep token costs predictable for you.

Next steps: if this looks good, can you confirm procurement contact and preferred final acceptance date range?

Thanks,
Jasmine Liu
Sr. AE, Redwood Inference
[jasmine_liu@redwood.com]
[Attachment: Helios_MAP_v3.xlsx (12KB); Evaluation_Checklist_v2.pdf (45KB)]

From: Sam Carter <scarter@helioshealth.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.com
Cc: Alex Ng <ang@helioshealth.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@helioshealth.com>
Date: Fri, 09 Mar 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed MAP & acceptance window for Q2 evaluation

Jasmine —

Appreciate the clear plan. Two immediate flags on our side that will push the acceptance window:

1) Procurement has a scheduled approval meeting only every other Thursday — that effectively adds a 7–10 business day gating window for contract sign-off.
2) Our security team is asking for a SOC 2 evidence bundle and a short architecture diagram for any cloud-connected endpoints; they treat these as blockers for production-ish evaluations.

We can still do the integration and smoke tests on your suggested timeline, but the final acceptance decision will likely slip by ~2 weeks unless procurement pre-approves via email or we can get an expedited review.

I'll loop Alex (engineering) and Procurement. Laura in Procurement will coordinate the approvals — she might ask for a short SOW and a procurement PO template.

—Sam

From: jasmine_liu@redwood.com
To: Alex Ng <ang@helioshealth.com>, Sam Carter <scarter@helioshealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, mina_haddad@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 12 Mar 2028 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed MAP & acceptance window for Q2 evaluation — suggested rebaseline

Alex / Sam —

Thanks for the quick take, Sam. Given procurement's cadence and the SOC2 evidence ask, recommended rebaseline below (I've highlighted which items are dependent on procurement/security):

- Revised Week 0 (prework): SOW and PO template submitted to Procurement (dependent) — target: 3/14
- Week 1–2: Integration + smoke tests (no change) — target: 3/20–3/31
- Week 3: Sec review & SOC2 evidence drop (dependent) — target: 4/3–4/7
- Week 4: Performance eval & business QA — target: 4/10–4/14
- Week 5: Acceptance window & contract signature — target: 4/17–4/21

Risk notes (short):
- If Procurement requires a PO signed before any environment is provisioned, we will need an expedited contract approval or a temporary test agreement; otherwise provisioning will be delayed up to three weeks.
- SOC2 evidence requests are usually a one-week turnaround if we share our packaged bundle and identify a single security contact at Helios.

Attachments: I've included a revised MAP (dates updated) and a zipped SOC2 evidence index. Ben, can you confirm capacity reservation for 4/10–4/14? Mina, can you prepare the SOC2 bundle for a drop?

Action items:
- Sam / Alex: confirm Procurement point-person (name + email) and whether Procurement accepts a provisional PO.
- Procurement: Laura — send preferred PO template by EOD 3/14 if possible.

If we can get procurement to acknowledge a provisional PO by 3/14, we should be able to keep the evaluation in April with only a one-week slip vs. the original plan.

Thanks,
Jasmine
Sr. AE, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Helios_MAP_v3_revised.xlsx (14KB); SOC2_evidence_stub.pdf (6KB)]

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: Sam Carter <scarter@helioshealth.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@helioshealth.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Mar 2028 14:45:00 -0700
Subject: Escalation: Helios MAP rebaseline + credit request guidance

Jasmine / Ben —

Looping in per Jasmine's ask. Quick read: Helios procurement cadence and SOC2 evidence create a high-probability path for a 1–3 week slip to the acceptance date. Before we escalate to the account execs and finance, please capture a compact risk log and a recommended concession ask (credits / extended trial) if Helios needs an earlier go-live commitment.

Suggested risk log (short):
- Risk: Procurement gating (bi-weekly committee)
  Impact: Up to 15 business days procurement delay
  Mitigation: Accept provisional PO; provide templated SOW; executive note to expedite

- Risk: Security evidence turnaround
  Impact: 5–7 business days
  Mitigation: Prepare SOC2 bundle; nominate single security contact; Redwood to provide temporary scoped test environment that doesn't require full evidence for sandbox access

Recommended concession for sales leadership review: one-time evaluation credit equal to 20% of one month of projected usage or a free two-week provisioning window if procurement signs an LOI/PO within 7 business days. This preserves momentum and keeps the cadence to April.

Marissa Cole
VP Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

---
